claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be processed to retain a homogeneous high-temperature BCC structure.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by competition between configurational entropy and enthalpic stabilization from chemical ordering.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the disordered BCC phase at high temperature.
Chemical ordering provides an enthalpic stabilization relative to the disordered state.
Ordering in this alloy is driven primarily by Al diffusion and rearrangement.
Cooling below a critical temperature reduces the configurational-entropy contribution enough to make the disordered BCC state less thermodynamically favorable.
Sufficient Al mobility below the critical temperature enables local atomic reordering.
Restricted Al diffusivity imposes the kinetic barrier to formation of the ordered phase.
An ordered phase nucleates in the BCC matrix when the ordering driving force becomes sufficient relative to the diffusional kinetic barrier.
Al diffusion is significantly activated in this alloy at approximately 650–750 °C.
Rapid quenching preserves the high-temperature BCC phase for use as a baseline.
A distinct ordering threshold temperature will occur in the investigated subcritical-temperature range.
Using fine temperature increments around a transition can improve experimental resolution of its temperature.
Ordering below the threshold will produce characteristic exothermic DSC peaks.
Ordering below the threshold will produce superlattice reflections in high-energy XRD.
Measured Al diffusion kinetics will correlate with the observed ordering transformation.
The critical temperature and ordering free-energy reduction depend on Al diffusion activation energies and microstructural heterogeneity.
Absence of both an exothermic peak and superlattice formation below the predicted critical temperature would falsify the hypothesis.
